parameters.notes: Projection recipe: new amount = statutory base amount x (C-CPI-U[year-1] / C-CPI-U[base year]) [for the 2016 base, the denominator is CPI-2016 x (C-CPI-U-2016/CPI-2016) = C-CPI-U-2016], rounded down. Practical shortcut that matches IRS within rounding: prior-year amount x ratio of consecutive C-CPI-U Sept-Aug averages, but always recompute from the statutory base to avoid compounding rounding errors. The OBBBA change gives the 10% and 12% bracket tops one extra year of inflation (2026 jump ~4.0% vs ~2.3% for higher brackets), which is visible in 2025->2026: 23,850->24,800 vs 394,600->403,550.

flags: SENIOR DEDUCTION SECTION: it is IRC §151(d)(5)(C), added by OBBBA §70103(a) - NOT §151(f). The brief's guess was wrong.

SENIOR DEDUCTION PHASE-OUT IS PER PERSON: the 6% reduction applies to each $6,000 (Schedule 1-A line 35 is entered once for each qualifying spouse), so an MFJ couple both 65+ loses $0.12 per $1 of MAGI over $150,000; zero at $250,000. If only one spouse qualifies, zero at $250,000 too (6% of $100,000).

2025 STANDARD DEDUCTION CHANGED MID-YEAR: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 said $15,000/$30,000; OBBBA (July 4, 2025) raised it to $15,750/$31,500, confirmed by Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.01 and the 2025 Form 1040 instructions. Use the OBBBA numbers. The 2025 additional 65+ amounts ($1,600/$2,000) were NOT changed.

BRACKET INDEXING CHANGED BY OBBBA §70101(b): the 10% and 12% bracket tops now index from 2016 instead of 2017, so they grow differently from the higher brackets. An engine that applies one inflation factor to all thresholds will drift. 2026 shows it: 10%/12% tops +3.98%/+3.97%, 22%+ thresholds +2.27%.
SINGLE vs MFS rounding: single brackets round to $25 (not $50) under §1(j)(3)(B)(ii), which is why single shows $201,775 and $256,225.
LTCG 15% ceiling for single ($545,500 in 2026) is a separate §1(j)(5)(B) number, not tied to any ordinary bracket edge; don't derive it from brackets.

SALT MFS floor: statute's $10,000 floor is on the 'applicable limitation amount', which §164(b)(6) then halves for MFS; IRS 2025 Schedule A worksheet confirms MFS floor = $5,000 (worksheet line 9 then 'half the amount on line 9'). Single and MFJ get the SAME $40,000 cap (no doubling).

SALT 2027-2029 values are not published and the statute gives no rounding rule (101% of prior year). I computed exact values ($40,804; $41,212.04; $41,624.16; thresholds $505,050; $510,100.50; $515,201.51) - treat as provisional until IRS publishes forms. Note the threshold keeps indexing after 2029 but the phasedown stops applying, so it's moot.
0.5% charitable floor is measured on 'contribution base' (AGI without NOL carrybacks), not AGI, though they are the same for nearly all retirees.

QCDs are not 'charitable contributions' for §170 (excluded from income, §408(d)(8)(E)), so neither the 0.5% floor nor the 2/37 limit touches them - a planning advantage, but this is my reading of the statute structure, not a quote from IRS guidance.
Age-55 separation exception does NOT apply to IRAs (§72(t)(3)(A)). The 'year you turn 55' timing comes from IRS guidance I did not fetch here; the statute only says 'after attainment of age 55'.

US CODE CURRENCY: uscode.house.gov (OLRC) was in maintenance mode; it reports being current through P.L. 119-120 (Oct 7, 2026). I read unchanged sections (§§1(f), 63, 72(t), 86, 170(p), 213, 408(d)(8), 1411) from govinfo's 2023 USC edition and applied OBBBA amendments from the enacted P.L. 119-21 text. I found no evidence of a later 2025-2026 law changing these parameters, but could not positively confirm against a current consolidated Code.
Rev. Proc. 2025-32 itself warns: if Code amendments for 2025 or 2026 are enacted after Oct 9, 2025, its adjustments may not apply. None found.
